results.title: Gumbel-Softmax Trick
results.content: * Gumbel-Softmax is a differentiable reparameterization technique that approximates categorical sampling, enabling efficient backpropagation in neural networks. The Gumbel-Softmax trick is a reparameterization technique that enables differentiable surrogate sampling from categorical distributions, allowing for efficient backpropagation through discrete latent variables in stochastic neural networks. The Gumbel-Softmax trick provides a pathwise gradient estimator by constructing a continuous, differentiable approximation to the categorical sample, leveraging the reparameterization trick previously successful with Gaussian latent variables (Jang et al., 2016). In structured tasks such as predicting the lower half of MNIST digits given the upper half, the Gumbel-Softmax estimator enables efficient sampling from discrete latent variables, outperforming alternatives—including score-function (SF), DARN, MuProp, and baseline straight-through estimators—in terms of negative log-likelihood (Jang et al., 2016). The Gumbel-Softmax trick provides a continuous, temperature-controlled, and differentiable relaxation of categorical sampling, enabling low-variance, pathwise gradient estimation in deep learning settings with discrete latent variables.

results.title: Generalized Gumbel-Softmax gradient estimator for generic discrete random variables - ScienceDirect
results.content: Generalized Gumbel-Softmax gradient estimator for generic discrete random variables - ScienceDirect Skip to main contentSkip to article Volume 196, October 2025, Pages 148-155 Generalized Gumbel-Softmax gradient estimator for generic discrete random variables Author links open overlay panel Weonyoung Joo a, Dongjun Kim b, Seungjae Shin c, Il-Chul Moon d * •The paper is a study on the stochastic gradient estimator, which generalizes the Gumbel-Softmax trick, namely GenGS. * •The proposed GenGS trick can reparameterize random variables which are following the generic discrete distributions. * •The GenGS reparameterizer has low bias and variance compared to other stochastic gradient estimators in the experiments. Stochastic gradient estimators of discrete random variables, such as the Gumbel-Softmax reparameterization trick for Bernoulli and categorical distributions, are widely explored. This paper proposes a generalized version of the Gumbel-Softmax stochastic gradient estimator. The proposed method is able to reparameterize generic discrete distributions, not restricted to the Bernoulli and the categorical, and it enables learning on large-scale stochastic computational graphs with discrete random nodes. Meanwhile, the reparameterization estimators result in biased gradients with low variances [4], but they require the _differentiable non-centered parameterization_ [5] of random variables. Meanwhile, for the discrete random variables which follow Bernoulli or categorical distributions, the SF-based methods are widely explored since the reparameterization method cannot directly work due to the non-differentiability. This paper proposes a generalized version of the Gumbel-Softmax trick, which can reparameterize the broader ranges of discrete distributions, not limited to the Bernoulli and the categorical. The proposed Generalized Gumbel-Softmax (GenGS) is probabilistically grounded, and it utilizes (1) a truncation to finitize the infinite support of the discrete distributions; and (2) a transformation that enables the generalization of the Gumbel-Softmax trick. The GenGS reparameterization trick results in low bias and variance compared to other stochastic gradient estimators, and it leads to better optimum points in our experiments. We enumerate stochastic gradient estimators which can be utilized for generic discrete random variables. GenGS utilizes the truncation of distribution support and the linear transformation to generalize the Gumbel-Softmax trick, specialized for reparameterizing categorical random variables. ### REBAR: Low-variance, unbiased gradient estimates for discrete latent variable models ### Adv. Neural Inf. Process.

results.content: When validation data are available, the non-iterative *regression calibration* (RC) method can be used to obtain approximately consistent point and interval linear, logistic and Cox regression model parameter estimates with measurement error in one or more continuous covariates, provided certain assumptions are satisfied (Prentice 1982; Fuller 1987; Armstrong, Whittemore et al. In Rosner *et al.*’s version of regression calibration, a standard multiple regression model is used to estimate the uncorrected point and interval estimates of the parameters, and these are bias-corrected using an estimate of the slopes from a linear measurement error model for the true exposure given the surrogate obtained from the validation data. Thus, there is a need to extend regression calibration to apply when the requirement for homoscedasticity of the measurement error model variance is violated, and to compare this extension to several less restrictive iterative approaches, including maximum likelihood and semi-parametric efficient estimating equations (Robins, Hsieh et al.
